hook: Researchers are using a $25,000 National Endowment for the Humanities grant to uncover lost Jewish manuscripts.

sections.voiceover: Researchers are using a $25,000 National Endowment for the Humanities grant to uncover lost Jewish manuscripts.
sections.visual_cue: Close-up of an ancient, weathered leather book spine on a wooden library table.
b_roll: Macro shot of antique book binding

sections.voiceover: Will terahertz imaging finally reveal the Jewish texts hidden inside these 1492 Spanish book bindings?
sections.visual_cue: Split screen showing a laboratory scanner and a 15th-century map of the Iberian Peninsula.

sections.voiceover: Jewish communities were expelled from the Iberian Peninsula in 1492, leaving behind books repurposed as bindings.
sections.visual_cue: Slow zoom into a dark, layered parchment texture.

sections.voiceover: Dr. Leor Jacobi and Prof. David Citrin use terahertz imaging to scan these historic, repurposed artifacts. This technology successfully reveals the hidden medieval texts trapped inside the 1492 Spanish book bindings.
sections.visual_cue: Portraits of the researchers overlaid with a digital terahertz scan effect.

sections.voiceover: The Georgia Institute of Technology and Bar-Ilan University launched this project on October 1, 2026.
sections.visual_cue: Wide shot of an ancient book resting on a shelf in a dimly lit archive.
